pre_knowledge_questions.text: Do you know your attachment style?
Do you know your primary love language?
Have you ever been to couples or individual therapy?

core_questions.text_mode_a: When my partner makes a mistake, I tend to focus on what they did wrong rather than the specific situation.
core_questions.text_mode_b: In past relationships, I tended to focus on what my partner did wrong rather than the specific situation.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Criticism subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner forgot to do something you asked them to do earlier this week. What's your most likely reaction?
core_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner forgot to do something you asked them to do earlier that week. What was your most likely reaction?

options.text: Roll my eyes or use a sarcastic tone like, 'Of course you forgot. Why am I not surprised?'
Feel frustrated and say, 'You always forget things I ask you to do.'
Mention it calmly and ask if there's a way to remember next time.

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Contempt subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: When my partner brings up a concern, I find myself explaining why it's not really my fault.
core_questions.text_mode_b: When my partner brought up a concern, I would find myself explaining why it wasn't really my fault.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Defensiveness subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: During a heated argument, how do you typically respond when you feel overwhelmed?
core_questions.text_mode_b: During heated arguments in past relationships, how did you typically respond when you felt overwhelmed?

options.text: I shut down completely -- go silent, leave the room, or stare blankly.
I ask for a short break but come back to the conversation later.
I stay engaged even though it's uncomfortable, trying to talk through it.
I get more intense and push harder to resolve things immediately.

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Stonewalling subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: I can name my partner's current biggest worry or stressor right now.
core_questions.text_mode_b: I could name my partner's biggest worry or stressor at the time.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman Love Maps Questionnaire

core_questions.text_mode_a: Which would make you feel more loved right now?
core_questions.text_mode_b: Which would have made you feel more loved?

forced_choices.text: My partner spending an uninterrupted evening with me, fully present
My partner writing me a heartfelt note about what I mean to them

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Chapman Love Languages Profile

core_questions.text_mode_a: I worry that my partner doesn't care about me as much as I care about them.
core_questions.text_mode_b: I worried that my partner didn't care about me as much as I cared about them.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 1, 5 - Anxiety subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: I feel uncomfortable when my partner wants to be very close emotionally.
core_questions.text_mode_b: I felt uncomfortable when my partner wanted to be very close emotionally.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 19, 23 - Avoidance subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner is running 30 minutes late and hasn't texted. What goes through your mind first?
core_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner was running 30 minutes late and hadn't texted. What went through your mind first?

options.text: Something terrible must have happened. I feel a knot in my stomach.
I feel annoyed and a bit anxious, but I try to distract myself.
They're probably just stuck in traffic. I'll text them to check in.
I barely notice and keep doing what I was doing.

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from BFI-K Items 4, 9 - Neuroticism subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: I can easily list several things I genuinely admire about my partner.
core_questions.text_mode_b: I could easily list several things I genuinely admired about my partner.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman Fondness & Admiration System

core_questions.text_mode_a: Which gesture would mean more to you?
core_questions.text_mode_b: Which gesture would have meant more to you?

forced_choices.text: My partner giving me a long, warm hug after a hard day
My partner taking care of a chore I've been dreading

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Chapman Love Languages Profile

core_questions.text_mode_a: When my partner is away, I find it hard to stop thinking about whether they're thinking of me.
core_questions.text_mode_b: When my partner was away, I found it hard to stop thinking about whether they were thinking of me.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 2, 14 - Anxiety subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: When we disagree, I sometimes think my partner is just being foolish or clueless.
core_questions.text_mode_b: When we disagreed, I sometimes thought my partner was just being foolish or clueless.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Contempt subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: You and your partner planned a weekend trip. How do you typically approach the planning?
core_questions.text_mode_b: You and your partner planned a weekend trip. How did you typically approach the planning?

options.text: I create a detailed itinerary with reservations, timelines, and backup plans.
I handle the big things (hotel, transport) and leave the rest open.
I suggest the idea but let my partner handle the details.
I prefer to be spontaneous -- we'll figure it out when we get there.

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from BFI-K Items 3, 8 - Conscientiousness subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: I prefer not to share my deepest feelings with my partner.
core_questions.text_mode_b: I preferred not to share my deepest feelings with my partner.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 25, 27 - Avoidance subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner points out something interesting while you're scrolling your phone. What do you usually do?
core_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner pointed out something interesting while you were scrolling your phone. What did you usually do?

options.text: I look up, engage with what they said, and respond with interest.
I glance up briefly, say 'oh cool,' and go back to my phone.
I keep looking at my phone and maybe grunt an acknowledgment.
I don't really register that they said anything.

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman Turning Toward vs. Away observation coding

core_questions.text_mode_a: In general, how satisfied are you with your relationship?
core_questions.text_mode_b: In general, how satisfied were you with your relationship?
core_questions.source_instrument: CSI-4 Item 1 (global satisfaction)

core_questions.text_mode_a: On your birthday, which would feel more special?
core_questions.text_mode_b: On your birthday, which would have felt more special?

forced_choices.text: A thoughtful, personalized gift my partner picked out just for me
My partner planning a full day of activities we enjoy together

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Chapman Love Languages Profile

core_questions.text_mode_a: I usually try to see things from my partner's perspective, even when we disagree.
core_questions.text_mode_b: I usually tried to see things from my partner's perspective, even when we disagreed.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from BFI-K Items 2, 7 - Agreeableness subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner left dishes in the sink again. You're frustrated. What do you say?
core_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner left dishes in the sink again. You were frustrated. What did you say?

options.text: 'You never clean up after yourself. You're so inconsiderate.'
'The dishes are still in the sink and it bugs me. Can we figure out a system?'
'I noticed the dishes are there. I'd appreciate it if you could get to them soon.'

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Criticism subscale (complaint vs criticism)

core_questions.text_mode_a: After a disagreement, I need reassurance that my partner still loves me before I can fully move on.
core_questions.text_mode_b: After a disagreement, I needed reassurance that my partner still loved me before I could fully move on.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 6, 8 - Anxiety subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: How often do you think things between you and your partner are going well?
core_questions.text_mode_b: How often did you think things between you and your partner were going well?
core_questions.source_instrument: CSI-4 Item 2 (frequency of positive sentiment)

core_questions.text_mode_a: When conflicts get intense, I emotionally check out even if I'm still physically present.
core_questions.text_mode_b: When conflicts got intense, I emotionally checked out even if I was still physically present.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Stonewalling subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: When you're feeling down, which would comfort you more?
core_questions.text_mode_b: When you were feeling down, which would have comforted you more?

forced_choices.text: My partner holding my hand or cuddling with me in silence
My partner telling me specific things they love and appreciate about me

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Chapman Love Languages Profile

core_questions.text_mode_a: Small relationship setbacks tend to affect my mood for a long time.
core_questions.text_mode_b: Small relationship setbacks tended to affect my mood for a long time.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from BFI-K Items 4, 14 - Neuroticism subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner is going through a really tough time and is visibly upset. What's your instinct?
core_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner was going through a really tough time and was visibly upset. What was your instinct?

options.text: I pull them close and ask them to tell me everything.
I offer comfort but also give them space if they need it.
I try to fix the problem practically rather than getting into the emotions.
I feel awkward and unsure of what to do, so I keep a bit of distance.

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 21, 31 - Avoidance subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: My relationship with my partner makes me happy.
core_questions.text_mode_b: My relationship with my partner made me happy.
core_questions.source_instrument: CSI-4 Item 3 (relationship happiness)

core_questions.text_mode_a: I follow through on promises I make to my partner, even small ones.
core_questions.text_mode_b: I followed through on promises I made to my partner, even small ones.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from BFI-K Items 3, 13 - Conscientiousness subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: When my partner is upset with me, my first reaction is to think of reasons why they're wrong to feel that way.
core_questions.text_mode_b: When my partner was upset with me, my first reaction was to think of reasons why they were wrong to feel that way.
core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Defensiveness subscale

core_questions.text_mode_a: Which would make you feel most appreciated?
core_questions.text_mode_b: Which would have made you feel most appreciated?

forced_choices.text: My partner surprising me with a small, meaningful gift 'just because'
My partner cooking dinner and handling cleanup so I can relax

core_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Chapman Love Languages Profile

core_questions.text_mode_a: I have a warm and comfortable relationship with my partner.
core_questions.source_instrument: CSI-4 Item 4 (warmth/comfort)

core_questions.text_mode_a: How rewarding is your relationship with your partner?
core_questions.source_instrument: CSI-4 supplemental (reward/cost ratio)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: When I'm upset, I tend to bring up a list of past grievances rather than sticking to the current issue.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: When I was upset, I tended to bring up a list of past grievances rather than sticking to the current issue.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Criticism subscale (kitchen-sinking)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner handled a social situation in a way you found embarrassing. How do you bring it up later?
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner handled a social situation in a way you found embarrassing. How did you bring it up later?

options.text: 'I felt awkward when that happened. Can we talk about it?'
'Why do you always have to do things like that?'
'You embarrassed me. You clearly don't care how I feel.'

follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Criticism subscale
follow_up_questions.text_prompt: Is there anything about how you handle frustration in relationships that you'd like your report to address?

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: I use words like 'always' or 'never' when describing my partner's behavior during conflicts.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: I used words like 'always' or 'never' when describing my partner's behavior during conflicts.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Criticism subscale (generalizing)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: I sometimes mock or mimic my partner's words or mannerisms when I'm frustrated with them.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: I sometimes mocked or mimicked my partner's words or mannerisms when I was frustrated with them.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Contempt subscale (mockery)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: Deep down, I sometimes feel like I'm smarter or more capable than my partner.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: Deep down, I sometimes felt like I was smarter or more capable than my partner.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Contempt subscale (superiority)
follow_up_questions.text_prompt: Is there anything about how respect shows up in your relationship that you'd like your report to address?

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner shares an idea you think is unrealistic. What's your gut reaction?
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner shared an idea you thought was unrealistic. What was your gut reaction?

options.text: I listen and ask questions, even if I have doubts.
I point out the flaws but try to be constructive.
I can't help but think 'here we go again' and let it show on my face.

follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Contempt subscale

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: When my partner criticizes me, I immediately think of something they do wrong too.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: When my partner criticized me, I immediately thought of something they did wrong too.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Defensiveness subscale (cross-complaining)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner says, 'You forgot to call the plumber like you said you would.' How do you respond?
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner said, 'You forgot to call the plumber like you said you would.' How did you respond?

options.text: 'You're right, I dropped the ball. I'll do it now.'
'I've been swamped with work. You could have called too, you know.'
'Well, you forgot to pick up the dry cleaning last week, so...'

follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Defensiveness subscale
follow_up_questions.text_prompt: Is there anything about how you handle being called out that you'd like your report to address?

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: I find it hard to say 'you're right' or 'I'm sorry' during an argument, even when I know I should.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: I found it hard to say 'you're right' or 'I'm sorry' during an argument, even when I knew I should.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Defensiveness subscale (inability to accept influence)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: During tense conversations, I sometimes feel physically overwhelmed -- racing heart, tightness in my chest, or a strong urge to flee.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: During tense conversations, I sometimes felt physically overwhelmed -- racing heart, tightness in my chest, or a strong urge to flee.
follow_up_questions.subtext: This describes 'diffuse physiological arousal' (DPA), which Gottman's research links to stonewalling.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Stonewalling subscale (DPA indicator)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: My partner would say I 'go cold' or become unreachable during conflicts.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: My partner would have said I 'went cold' or became unreachable during conflicts.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Stonewalling subscale (partner perception)
follow_up_questions.text_prompt: Is there anything about how you handle emotional overwhelm that you'd like your report to address?

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner wants to talk through a conflict right now, but you're feeling flooded. What do you do?
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner wanted to talk through a conflict right then, but you were feeling flooded. What did you do?

options.text: I say 'I need 20 minutes to calm down and then I'll be ready to talk.'
I go silent and hope they stop talking.
I leave the room without explanation.
I stay but I'm not really present -- I nod along without processing.

follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from Gottman FHQ - Stonewalling subscale (repair attempts)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: I often wonder if my partner would leave me for someone better.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: I often wondered if my partner would leave me for someone better.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 4, 18 - Anxiety subscale (abandonment fear)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: I check my phone frequently to see if my partner has texted or called when we're apart.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: I checked my phone frequently to see if my partner had texted or called when we were apart.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 10, 16 - Anxiety subscale (proximity seeking)
follow_up_questions.text_prompt: Is there anything about how you handle separation or distance in relationships that you'd like your report to address?

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner seems a little distant today but says 'nothing's wrong.' What goes through your mind?
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner seemed a little distant that day but said 'nothing's wrong.' What went through your mind?

options.text: They're probably just having an off day. I give them space.
I feel uneasy and try to figure out if I did something wrong.
I feel a spike of panic and keep asking if everything is okay between us.

follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 6, 8 - Anxiety subscale (hyperactivation)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: I feel most comfortable in relationships when there's a certain amount of emotional distance.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: I felt most comfortable in relationships when there was a certain amount of emotional distance.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 29, 33 - Avoidance subscale (deactivation)

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: I pride myself on being self-reliant and not needing my partner too much.
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: I prided myself on being self-reliant and not needing my partner too much.
follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 35, 36 - Avoidance subscale (compulsive self-reliance)
follow_up_questions.text_prompt: Is there anything about how you handle closeness and vulnerability in relationships that you'd like your report to address?

follow_up_questions.text_mode_a: Your partner wants to have a deep conversation about the future of your relationship. How do you feel?
follow_up_questions.text_mode_b: Your partner wanted to have a deep conversation about the future of your relationship. How did you feel?

options.text: I welcome the conversation -- it feels like a sign of a healthy relationship.
I'm willing but feel a bit uneasy about going too deep.
I feel trapped and want to change the subject or postpone.
I shut down internally -- these conversations feel threatening.

follow_up_questions.source_instrument: Adapted from ECR-R Items 25, 27 - Avoidance subscale (intimacy discomfort)
